sandbox.summary: The patch was applied in an isolated Docker container and pytest exited with code 0. Two tests were collected and both passed (test_math_utils.py::test_add and test_math_utils.py::test_multiply), with no failures, errors, skips, or warnings. The run took 0.01s on Python 3.11.17 with pytest 9.1.1. Verdict: PASS. Caveat: the suite is small (2 tests), so this verdict only covers the behavior those tests exercise.

patch.explanation: multiply() in sample-app/math_utils.py was implemented using addition (`a + b`) rather than multiplication, so multiply(2, 4) returned 6 instead of 8 and failed test_multiply. The one-line change to `return a * b` fixes the root cause. The test expectations (multiply(2, 4) == 8 and multiply(3, 3) == 9) are correct and both pass with this change. test_add and all other code are left untouched.
